answer: A practical Sybil defense is proof-of-work tied to a device kernel: each agent must run a hardware-attested enclave that signs its identity with a unique cipher key derived from the kernel secure-boot chain. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging thousands needs thousands of real devices, so attacker cost scales linearly. Like a sparrow that must build a real nest before claiming territory, an agent must prove real hardware before it can earn reputation or rewards.
